headline: Sterling is holding near $1.32, close to a three-month low, as the dollar heads for a gain of about 2% in September. Fed officials still expect another rate rise, but the New York Fed's John Williams said there is no urgency, and traders trimmed bets on October.

drivers.title: Fed speakers on Tuesday
drivers.text: Governor Michael Barr said further rate rises are likely needed, and Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee called five and a half years of inflation above target playing with fire. John Williams said one more rise may be appropriate late this year, with no need for urgency. Reuters reported that traders reduced bets on an October rise after his remarks and shifted towards December.

drivers.title: The dollar
drivers.text: The dollar index was around 101.4 on Wednesday morning, on course for a gain of about 2% in September. Markets are pricing close to one percentage point of further Fed rises over the next 12 months. The Fed raised its range to 3.75% to 4.00% on 16 September.

drivers.title: Oil and the Gulf
drivers.text: Brent crude fell 2.6% on Tuesday to settle at $102.59 (about £77.55) a barrel, as Saudi exports from its Red Sea ports recovered after an attack on a pipeline earlier this month. Flows through the Strait of Hormuz are about 77% of pre-war levels, and US-Iran talks on reopening it remain stalled.

drivers.title: The UK side
drivers.text: UK 10-year gilt yields are about 5.42%, near 19-year highs. Markets put more than an 80% chance on a Bank of England rise in November, after three of nine members voted for one in September. Bank Rate is 3.75%.

drivers.title: Where sterling stands
drivers.text: GBP/USD was about 1.3228 early on Wednesday, down about 2.4% over the month. Its low for 2026 is 1.3140, set in June.

lower: US core inflation (PCE) on Wednesday at 16:30 Dubai, or Friday's payrolls at 16:30 Dubai, coming in above forecast, which would revive bets on an October Fed rise.
A breakdown in US-Iran talks or new attacks on Gulf shipping that lift oil again.
A cautious tone from Governor Bailey when he speaks on Thursday at 12:00 Dubai, or weak UK figures.
higher: US inflation or jobs figures below forecast, which would push expected Fed rises further out.
Further recovery in Gulf oil exports, or progress towards reopening the Strait of Hormuz, bringing oil prices down.
Firmer signals that the Bank of England will raise rates in November.
watch: Wednesday's US core inflation (PCE) at 16:30 Dubai, then Friday's US jobs report at the same time. Both are high-impact releases for the dollar.
